subject: Re: Private deployment - evidence collector & forwarder design
messages:
From: Olivia Barnes <olivia.barnes@acmefin.com>
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.com
Cc: Acme Fintech SecOps <secops@acmefin.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2026 14:23:00 -0700
Subject: Observability in our private deployment — collectors / forwarders / evidence packaging

Diego,

Thanks for taking this on. We’re finalizing the security requirements for the private deployment (VPC + on-prem gateway) and need clarity on how Redwood can surface logs/metrics/traces to our SIEM without exposing a public endpoint. High level asks from SecOps: 

- Supported export modes: push (syslog/tcp/tls), pull (S3 ingestion), or a proxy agent that runs in our VPC?
- Evidence packaging: do you provide signed bundles (per-hour/day) containing request headers, trace ids, and retention hashes for audit?
- Tracing: OTLP/Zipkin endpoints are not reachable outside our network. Can an agent forward traces to an internal collector?
- Backpressure & buffering: how do you guarantee no data loss if connectivity to Acme SIEM is interrupted?
- KMS / key handling: we must use our CMK for HMAC signing of evidence.

Attached is our SIEM questionnaire (acme-siem-questionnaire.xlsx). Can you propose 2-3 architecture patterns (minimal risk -> more advanced) and call out tradeoffs? Our target timeline is a review call next week.

—Olivia
Olivia Barnes
Head of Security Engineering, Acme Fintech
olivia.barnes@acmefin.com

From: diego_fernandez@redwood.com
To: Olivia Barnes <olivia.barnes@acmefin.com>
Cc: Acme Fintech SecOps <secops@acmefin.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2026 15:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observability in our private deployment — collectors / forwarders / evidence packaging

Olivia — thanks, this is a good starting point. I’ve sketched three viable patterns and attached a short design doc (redwood-private-forwarder-design.pdf) plus config examples. Summary below; happy to walk through on a call.

1) Local forwarder (recommended, low friction)
  - A small Redwood-provided forwarder runs in your VPC (ECS/VM).
  - Forwards logs/metrics/traces to your SIEM via syslog over TLS or to an internal Kafka/S3 bucket for ingestion.
  - Buffering: local disk queue + configurable retention; backpressure triggers local throttling and token-limited retry.
  - Evidence bundles: forwarder can assemble hourly bundles, sign with a customer-supplied HMAC key (you control CMK), and upload to a locked S3 path for audit.

2) Push-to-S3 / Pull-internal (higher isolation)
  - Redwood writes encrypted, signed bundles to an S3 endpoint (or NFS) inside your network.
  - Your SIEM pulls bundles on a scheduled job; no outbound connections from your SIEM required.
  - Tradeoff: slightly higher latency for real-time alerting, simpler compliance.

3) Proxy + Secure Tunnel (most real-time, more operational coordination)
  - Site-to-site tunnel to a Redwood ingestion endpoint with mutual TLS and IP allowlisting.
  - Redwood performs tokenized per-tenant routing and pushes events into your SIEM over a dedicated connector (Splunk/QRadar).
  - Tradeoff: fastest for streaming traces, requires network approvals and SLA negotiation.

Tracing: all patterns can accept OTLP/Zipkin locally. The forwarder exposes OTLP to local apps and converts/forwards to the method of your choice.

KMS: we don’t hold your CMK. We support passing an HMAC key via secrets manager in your VPC or providing a signing callback that uses your HSM.

Next steps: propose 45 min design review. Availability: Thu 6/17 or Mon 6/21 afternoon (PDT).

Diego Fernandez
Technical PM — Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Diego — quick tech addendum for the call. Quoting your summary above for context:

On Tue, 15 Jun 2026 at 15:05 Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com> wrote:
> 1) Local forwarder (recommended, low friction)
>   - A small Redwood-provided forwarder runs in your VPC (ECS/VM).
>   - Forwards logs/metrics/traces to your SIEM via syslog over TLS or to an internal Kafka/S3 bucket for ingestion.

Notes / recommendations from infra: 
- Forwarder implementation: go-daemon with circular file queue + LZ4 compression. Default disk cap 20GB, configurable.
- Delivery guarantees: at-least-once with dedupe headers (X-Redwood-Event-Id). For SIEM ingest jobs that cannot dedupe, we’ll provide sequence + MD5 manifest.
- Evidence signing: we support two modes: (a) local HMAC using a customer key stored in your Secrets Manager, or (b) Redwood signs a manifest and you validate via an exchange public key. Mode (a) meets the CMK requirement.
- Networking: forwarder binds to loopback OTLP endpoint; no public ports. Outbound only options use TLS with cert pinning to our collector (if you choose pattern 3).
- Traces: OTLP gRPC recommended for span fidelity. Forwarder will batch spans per 1s or 10s window depending on latency targets.
- SIEM connectors: we’ve validated Splunk HEC (token auth over HTTPS) and syslog-tls to ArcSight/SNARE in customer labs. QRadar ingestion requires SAX/CEF formatting — we can supply formatting templates.
- Operational hooks: healthcheck metrics to local Prometheus endpoint + readiness that can be scraped by your cluster.

Action items for the call: (1) Olivia to confirm allowed outbound hosts/IPs (if any), (2) ACME to confirm desired evidence cadence (hourly/daily), (3) Redwood to demo forwarder config and sample signed bundle.

Hannah
Senior Infra Eng, Redwood

Attached: config examples (collector-config-examples.yaml) and the design doc.

Proposed 45-min review: Thu 6/17 10:30-11:15 PDT (we can slide to 11:00 if needed). Please confirm and we’ll send a calendar invite with an agenda:

  - Evidence signing & KMS approach (10m)

  - Q&A / next steps (10m)

If you prefer stricter isolation, we’ll scope Pattern 2 for the follow-on sprint and detail the S3 pull job.

Thanks,
